facts.text: Marathon Valley was deployed at Meridiani Planum during Opportunity (MER-B) in 2015.

In March 2015, Opportunity reached Marathon Valley on the rim of Endeavour Crater, having driven 42.195 km — a full marathon distance. The valley contained clay minerals detected from orbit by the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter. Clay minerals form in near-neutral water, suggesting this area once had conditions more hospitable to life.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Contained clay minerals that form only in near-neutral pH water, suggesting this area once had conditions hospitable to life — the gentlest water environment found by a rover.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Meridiani Planum.
Marathon Valley marks where Opportunity completed a full marathon distance (42.195 km) on another planet, a milestone in human exploration.
